tools.name: search_papers
tools.description: Search peer-reviewed and preprint literature across all scientific disciplines (OpenAlex, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC), deduplicated and ranked by study design and citations. Returns abstracts, evidence level (meta-analysis, systematic-review, rct, review, cohort, empirical, preclinical, other) and a citation/venue band (`tier`: top, high, standard, emerging — not a JCR quartile) and scientific `domain`. YOU classify each paper's stance and synthesize.

tools.name: clarify_search_scope
tools.description: Clarification loop for broad queries: says whether a query is too broad (needs >= 2 of: 5+ meaningful words, boolean operators/quoted phrase, time constraint, method + outcome) and returns 3 domain-specific multiple-choice questions. Ask the user, then call again with `answers` ({"q1": option label or 1-based index, ...}) to get `refined_query` and `recommended_filters` (year_min, study_types, sources, sort) for search_papers. Skip it when the user already gave a precise query.

tools.name: get_paper
tools.description: Get full record and abstract of a paper by cached ID, DOI, PMID, OpenAlex ID, arXiv ID, or Semantic Scholar ID. Includes its scientific `domain`; pass `domain` to override it.

tools.name: detect_paper_domain
tools.description: Detect a paper's scientific macro-domain (computer_science, biomedical, economics, general_stem) from arXiv categories, fields of study, PubMed indexing and title/abstract vocabulary, explaining the signals used. Use it to pick domain-appropriate evaluation criteria.

tools.name: scan_paper_artifacts
tools.description: Open-artifact radar: find code repositories (GitHub/GitLab/...), model weights (Hugging Face, Civitai, Kaggle, PyTorch Hub) and datasets (Zenodo, Figshare, OSF, Dataverse, HF datasets) linked from a paper, verify that the links are alive (HEAD, 5s timeout, max 20 URLs) and flag evasive 'available on request' statements. Set inspect_fulltext=true to also scan the open-access full text.

tools.name: get_paper_references
tools.description: Citation graph with influence ranking: papers this paper cites (`backward_citations`) and papers citing it (`forward_citations`), with title, year, venue, citation_count and Semantic Scholar's `is_influential` flag (OpenAlex fallback: >= 50 citations). Every returned `paper_id` is cached, so you can chain get_paper, get_paper_references or download_papers on it.

tools.name: compare_papers
tools.description: Comparative matrix of 1-10 papers (3-5 typical): for each paper extracts the core problem/hypothesis, methodology (design + domain + method sentence), datasets/benchmarks/population, key results/metrics (headline finding, %, p-values, AUC, F1, HR, ...) and declared limitations, then returns a Markdown table plus convergence and divergence summaries. Set inspect_fulltext=true to also mine open-access full text.

tools.name: get_thematic_insights
tools.description: Thematic synthesis of 1-20 papers across 3 cross-cutting axes (no isolated per-paper summaries): `consolidated_consensuses` (shared concepts, benchmarks and highest-level evidence), `methodological_tensions` (evidence-pyramid gaps, dataset/scale differences, open-artifact asymmetry, mixed results) and `emerging_future_work` (cross-referenced limitations and future work). Every statement cites [Author et al., Year]; `citations_map` maps each tag to paper ids.

tools.name: generate_research_hypotheses
tools.description: Autonomous research gap & hypothesis engine (#18): cross-analyzes 2-15 papers to detect methodological contradictions (`contradictions_found`) and unexplored synergies where one paper's method mitigates another's limitation (`unexplored_complementarities`), then formulates 1-`max_hypotheses` structured, testable `ResearchHypothesis` proposals with `source_papers` (>= 2), `proposed_methodology`, `required_baselines`, `target_datasets_or_population`, and `evaluation_metrics`.

tools.name: export_obsidian_notes
tools.description: Export papers as atomic Obsidian/Markdown notes (`<Year> - <FirstAuthor> - <ShortTitle>.md`) into `vault_dir` (inside the workspace; default ./obsidian): YAML frontmatter (title, paper_id, doi, year, authors, venue, domain, evidence_level, citations, open_access, has_code, has_weights, tags), TL;DR, key findings & methodology, open artifacts, [[wikilinks]] between the exported notes and a BibTeX block.

tools.name: suggest_boolean_queries
tools.description: Dynamic search expansion: mine acronyms (e.g. LoRA, GPTQ) and emerging technical terms from `paper_ids` (or from cached papers matching `query`) and return 3 ready-to-run boolean queries for search_papers: [1] precision deepening (AND), [2] synonym/method expansion (OR + AND), [3] noise exclusion (NOT).

tools.name: extract_benchmark_tables
tools.description: Benchmark table extractor: detects Markdown, LaTeX (tabular) and plain-text/PDF tables plus inline `Benchmark: value` pairs in the paper's open-access full text (abstract fallback), keeps the exact model-row x metric-column correspondence, normalizes metric names (gsm-8k -> GSM8K, human-eval -> HumanEval, acc -> Accuracy, ppl -> Perplexity, ...) and converts values like '84.5%' or '84.5 ± 0.3' to numbers. Returns `tables` and a cross-table `normalized_summary` (by_metric, best_by_metric).

tools.name: estimate_hardware_specs
tools.description: Hardware feasibility / inference footprint: detects the model size (7B, 1.5B, 350M, 8x7B MoE, '671B parameters with 37B activated', family defaults) and architecture (dense, moe, encoder_only, rnn_ssm), then computes FP16/INT8/INT4 weights, KV cache (2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x context x bytes) and recommended minimum VRAM (+15% overhead), extracts the authors' reported training hardware (e.g. '64 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs', 'TPU v4-1024') and classifies the operational tier (edge_consumer_gpu <= 16 GB, workstation <= 48 GB, datacenter_cluster) from the INT4 footprint. Override sizes with total_params_b / active_params_b.

tools.name: verify_paper_claims
tools.description: Evidence grounding with strict attribution: checks each claim (or, when `claims` is empty, the numeric/comparative sentences auto-extracted from the abstract/text) against the paper's literal text, indexed by page and table/section. Returns `status` verified (all numbers literally in the same passage), partially_supported (topic found, some numbers diverge) or extrapolated, with a mandatory citation tag '[pág. X, Tabela Y: "..."]' / '[pág. X, Seção Y: "..."]' or an explicit '[EXTRAPOLAÇÃO NÃO LITERAL ...]' warning. Use it before stating numbers from a paper.

tools.name: extract_paper_math
tools.description: Math & pseudocode extractor: finds equations (\begin{equation|align}, $$..$$, \[..\], inline $a = b$, plain-text 'L_total = ...' / 'Attention(Q, K, V) = ...') and algorithms (\begin{algorithm}, 'Algorithm N:' blocks). mode='latex' returns clean delimited LaTeX; mode='python' returns typed Python functions (`def equation_1(...) -> float` / `def algorithm_1(...) -> Any`, `import math`, original LaTeX in the docstring), always validated with ast.parse; mode='both' returns both.

tools.name: analyze_ablation_tables
tools.description: Ablation analyzer: locates ablation tables/lists (rows 'Full model' / 'Ours' / 'Baseline' and variants 'w/o X', 'without X', '- X', '+ X', 'no X'), takes the full model (else baseline) as reference and computes, per component and metric, delta and delta_percent, flags is_marginal (|Δ%| < 1%), ranks components by |Δ%| and emits warnings_and_alerts for marginal components and for a single component accounting for >= 60% of the total reported gain.

tools.name: extract_prompts_and_decoding
tools.description: Prompt & inference protocol extractor: finds prompt templates (after 'System Prompt:', 'User Prompt:', 'Prompt Template:', 'Instruction:', in code fences/quotes, or text with {variable}, {{variable}}, <context>, "Let's think step by step", "You are an expert") keeping placeholders verbatim and listing `variables`; extracts decoding hyperparameters (temperature, top_p, top_k, max_tokens, repetition_penalty, beam_size, seed, decoding_strategy) with literal evidence, and the JSON output schemas shown in the paper.

tools.name: detect_failure_modes
tools.description: Failure mode & critical assumption detector: scans Limitations, Error Analysis, Failure Cases, Discussion, Threats to Validity and Appendix (plus abstract/body) to classify failure modes into long_context, noise_sensitivity, out_of_distribution, latency_or_compute, sample_or_population_bias and general_limitation (with severity high/medium/low), extracts critical_assumptions, identifies baseline_superiority_scenarios (both from text and from benchmark tables where a baseline beats Ours), and extracts operational_limits.

tools.name: diff_arxiv_versions
tools.description: arXiv temporal version diff analyzer: fetches and compares two revisions of an arXiv preprint (e.g. v1 vs v2), tracking title and authorship changes, metric and table number deltas (`metric_deltas`), claim attenuations or strengthenings (`claim_shifts`), newly added baselines or datasets (`new_baselines_or_datasets`) and a structured `markdown_diff` report.

tools.name: review_paper
tools.description: Multi-persona peer-review committee (#17, #20): detects the paper's scientific domain (or uses `domain` override) and runs 3 specialized reviewer personas (NeurIPS/ICLR Theoretical, Skeptical Empirical, and Systems/Reproducibility for CS/AI; CONSORT/STROBE Clinical Trial Methodologist, Biostatistician, and Translational Safety Reviewer for Biomedical; Causal Identification Econometrician, Robustness Auditor, and Policy Economist for Economics) consolidated by a Meta-Reviewer into a PeerReviewReport with verdict, scores, cited flaws/omissions, and questions.

tools.name: review_paper_scientific
tools.description: Alias for review_paper: domain-adaptive 3-persona scientific peer-review committee (#17, #20).

tools.name: scaffold_implementation
tools.description: Polyglot code & experimental protocol scaffolder (#16, #21): translates a paper's mathematical formulations, architecture, econometric specification or clinical trial design into executable, ast-validated code + unit tests (PyTorch `nn.Module` with shape assertions for CS/AI; Statsmodels or R `fixest` panel + robustness matrix for Economics; CONSORT/STROBE operational checklist + ITT analytical pipeline for Biomedical/STEM).

tools.name: scaffold_paper_code
tools.description: Alias for scaffold_implementation (#16, #21): generates PyTorch, Statsmodels/R, or Clinical Protocol code + unit tests.

tools.name: recommend_citations
tools.description: Contextual citation recommender & infiller (#22): scans a draft paragraph or file (.md/.tex) for explicit `[CITATION NEEDED]` / `\cite{?}` markers and unsubstantiated empirical claims, retrieves 2-3 supporting papers per claim with explicit Portuguese justifications ('Este artigo de X et al. (Ano) comprova essa afirmação...'), inserts inline LaTeX or Markdown citations, and generates a deduplicated BibTeX block.

tools.name: synthesize_related_work
tools.description: Narrative Related Work synthesizer (#24): clusters 1-20 papers into thematic approach families (Architectural & Representation Foundations, Training/Optimization/Causal Identification, Efficiency/Scaling/Empirical Evaluation), writes comparative academic prose (While X..., Y..., whereas Z... — never isolated per-author lists), positions the user's `proposal` against the collective gap, and exports Markdown or `\section{Related Work}` LaTeX plus BibTeX.

tools.name: generate_manuscript_blueprint
tools.description: IMRaD manuscript blueprint generator (#23 Mode 1): generates a venue-adapted (neurips, icml, iclr, acl, ieee, nature, lancet, aer, general) structural template with paragraph-by-paragraph writing guidance and required elements in Markdown or LaTeX.

tools.name: audit_manuscript_draft
tools.description: Draft manuscript auditor (#23 Mode 2): audits a draft (.md/.tex in workspace or inline text) for weak or unsubstantiated claims, mathematical/terminological inconsistencies ($L$ vs $\mathcal{L}$), and reproducibility omissions (seeds, hyperparameters, sample size N, error bars, compute hardware).

tools.name: sanitize_bibtex
tools.description: BibTeX sanitizer & preprint-to-published resolver (#25): parses `.bib` files or text, upgrades arXiv/CoRR preprints (`@misc`) to their definitive peer-reviewed conference (`@inproceedings`) or journal (`@article`) venue with DOI, removes duplicates keeping the cleanest key, standardizes authors, escapes unescaped LaTeX (`&`, `%`, `_`), and protects acronyms (`{LLM}`, `{GPU}`).

tools.name: parse_and_draft_rebuttal
tools.description: Peer-review Rebuttal Copilot (#26): segments raw reviewer comments (`Reviewer 1`, `Reviewer 2`, ...) into numbered actionable points, classifies each objection, flags requests requiring new experiments (`requires_new_experiment=True`), and generates polite, evidence-backed Author Rebuttals in Markdown and LaTeX.

tools.name: audit_submission_readiness
tools.description: Pre-Submission & Desk-Reject Gatekeeper (#27): runs a 4-stage audit on a `.tex`, `.md`, or `.pdf` manuscript for the target `venue` — (1) Double-Blind Anonymity Audit (non-anonymous GitHub/HF URLs, `\author` blocks, PDF metadata, first-person self-citations), (2) Venue Checklist Engine, (3) Overclaiming Scanner, and (4) Mandatory Sections Check — returning a `readiness_score` (0-100) and `desk_reject_risk`.

tools.name: get_fulltext
tools.description: Fetch open-access full text (via OpenAlex, EuropePMC, arXiv, Unpaywall) and return excerpts relevant to `question`.

tools.name: query_fulltexts
tools.description: Query across multiple papers simultaneously for a specific question (uses full text when Open Access or abstract fallback). Ideal for conversing over a set of papers.

tools.name: citation_graph
tools.description: Papers this paper cites (references) and papers citing it (OpenAlex), automatically cached for follow-up.

tools.name: related_papers
tools.description: Find papers semantically similar to the target paper, papers it cites (references), or papers citing it. Supports filtering by study_types and year_min.

tools.name: download_papers
tools.description: Download Open Access PDFs for one or more paper IDs or DOIs into `output_dir` (inside the workspace; default: configured download_dir, ./papers).

tools.name: save_research_dossier
tools.description: Save a persistent research dossier (README.md, papers.json, references.bib) in `output_dir` (inside the workspace; default: configured research_dir, ./research) so the user can converse over the research documentation.

tools.name: list_research_dossiers
tools.description: List saved research dossiers available for follow-up conversation.

tools.name: get_research_dossier
tools.description: Load a saved research dossier (Markdown report and paper metadata) by slug or topic.

tools.name: export_papers
tools.description: Export papers as bibtex, ris or csv.

tools.name: evidence_meter
tools.description: Compute the Evidence Meter deterministically from YOUR stance classification of each paper: raw counts and percentages plus study-design-weighted percentages (meta-analysis 1.0 … preclinical 0.2). Use its output instead of computing percentages yourself.

tools.name: configure_noul
tools.description: View (no arguments) or update the persistent Noul configuration: contact email (enables Unpaywall and the OpenAlex/Crossref polite pool), workspace folder, and default download/research folders. `clear` resets it.
